text: Alex wants outside critic reviews checked for whether they find real issues or invent them, e.g. by planting known bugs and verifying every finding before acting on it.
When Alex says a mechanic should give 'a little' of something, tune it to a modest share, check that in a balance run, and say what was picked.

Cross-agent review calibration (concurrent RV-005, 10-10): with 3 bugs planted in one packet, Grok caught 3/3 and Codex 2/3 (missed the low one), neither invented anything, and between them they found 3 real unplanted bugs (one found by both); record in concurrent docs/reviews/RV-005-calibration.md.

Grok's track record as a hostile reviewer (concurrent RV-001..005): 5 of 17 findings invented, every one a confident 'X never happens' misread of a big diff; never act on a Grok or Codex finding before checking it against the code.

Grok and Codex complement each other on one packet: Grok was sharper on state leaking between screens/battles, Codex on timing and gaps against the stated goal; running both at a milestone is worth it.

Alex 10-10 on cross-agent reviews: catching hallucinations and agents keeping each other accountable is 'exactly the move'; calibrate reviewers with planted bugs (built from a throwaway worktree copy, plant catches logged outside findings.jsonl) and have a blind fresh agent re-verify contested findings.
